summary: Gate 1 evidence-preparation review of the PR299 Perlmutter archive against measured head acfd029a8d27898b5f165e02facd3c3bbc9c4ad2. The note and README are consistent with the compact evidence: paired medians, ranges, loop medians, the GPU BD1 order gap, paired MPI-wall change, setup medians, sustained windows, BD2 unlogged tails, completed-byte totals, memory peak/limit, monitor intervals, and reclaim counters all match the inspected JSON/CSV/log files. Execution order, PASS coverage, manifest/approval/review binding, build-option parity, and the verify_install before-only qualification were confirmed from the files. Scope qualifications (Run51 screen not equivalence, C1 blocking and unfixed, Run77 deferred, one stream per BD, no GDS, storage/reclaim limits, missing raw payloads) are stated accurately. No production code is touched. Three low, non-blocking documentation corrections are requested; none affect provenance or the measured result. Supplied validation evidence (offline verifier pass, four packaging tests, parse/bash -n checks, hash validation) was accepted as reported and not rerun.
checks: Paired table: campaign-summary.json medians/ranges/loop medians match the note for all six cases; CSV rows match slurm-61375111.out rates and MPI walls; verify_archive.py recomputes the same quantities.

GPU BD1 order analysis: head-second median +2.52%, head-first -2.79%, 5.31 point gap matches campaign-summary.json; paired MPI-wall change median -1.73%, range -10.47% to +4.81% recomputed from paired-timings.csv.
Setup medians 14.02 / 17.43 s recomputed from max-rank setup_seconds in the eight timed-r51-gpu-events-bd1 sample summaries.

Execution order: 60 PASS lines in slurm-61375111.out, 12 preflights then 48 timed samples in B/H, H/B, B/H, H/B order; no FAIL/ERROR/Traceback lines; stderr contains only the cudatoolkit module reload.
campaign-slurm-accounting.txt: COMPLETED, 0:0, 02:44:14, nid003260, lcls_g, gpu_premium, full node (cpu=128, gres/gpu=4, mem=229802M); consistent with the note and the 240.965 GB cgroup limit.

Sustained windows: BD1 late-half 66.58-69.17 ev/s and quarter ratios 0.923-0.977; BD2 43.36-51.13 and 0.767-0.941 match campaign-validation.json; BD2 rank event counts 4960-5040 vs last logged 4900/5000 give 0-80 unlogged tails.
Storage rollup: 4157 samples, peak 94005649408 bytes, zero memory.events, nonzero pgscan/pgsteal/refault deltas, monitor period 2.262-2.366 s, Lustre llite and PSI unavailable; matches the note.

Provenance binding: manifest base/head SHAs, manifest hash 1433a210... in status.json, review-approval-campaign.json and reviews/campaign-r1.json; reviewed_commit equals HEAD, verdict pass, no blocking findings; pilot digest b08dd643... agrees across approval and review.
worker.py line 67 calls verify_install once before the workload; runtime_provenance is recorded before (line 78) and after (line 168). The note's qualification of FINAL_REPORT.txt wording is correct.
input-verification-51.json ends with matches: true and lists ten SMD/bigdata entries; reference-51.json has available_events 17872 with the 10000-event prefix.

Build options: build-options-head.json shows release, optimization 3, debug false, b_lto true, b_ndebug true, c++20, build_daq false, prefix install-head; build logs show fresh scratch build/install trees.

Counts: SHA256SUMS 629 entries (+ itself = 630 files), archive-map.json 624 entries, SOURCE_SHA256SUMS 1171 entries; new files (note, README, verify_archive.py, test_verify_archive.py, archive-map.json, SHA256SUMS) are the six non-preserved files.
Scripts: 21 harness .py + 7 analysis .py + verify_archive.py + test_verify_archive.py = 30 Python files; campaign-job.sh and job.sh are the two shell wrappers.

Public-release scan: regex scan for passwords/secrets/tokens/private keys/email addresses over psana/psana/gpu found no matches; archive intentionally contains /global/homes/m/monarin and /pscratch/sd/m/monarin paths, account lcls_g, GPU UUID, node name and job IDs, as disclosed in the README; SOURCE_SHA256SUMS lists names and hashes of excluded iris balance and reviewer invocation files but not their contents.

Historical scripts: campaign-job.sh and job.sh carry absolute original paths and a frozen review gate (review_gate/check_frozen in perlmutter_screen.py) so a blind resubmission fails closed; README states do-not-submit and no adaptation.

.pre-commit-config.yaml confirms trailing-whitespace and end-of-file-fixer are the only format-mutating hooks; check-yaml, check-merge-conflict, mixed-line-ending, check-ast, debug-statements, check-added-large-files and cython-lint remain enabled.
Markdown links in the note and README resolve to existing files/directories in the checkout.
limitations: Could not read the worktree HEAD ref: /sdf/home/m/monarin/lcls2/.git/worktrees/review/HEAD is outside the restricted working directory. The reviewed SHA is taken from the task statement and the git status snapshot (344dd1437, 'docs(gpu): archive PR299 Perlmutter performance evidence').
No commands were run and no SHA-256 values were computed. Verifier pass, four packaging tests, 30-file parse, bash -n, hash validation and pre-commit outcomes are accepted from the supplied context.

Only a subset of the 60 sample directories was inspected in detail (timed-r51-gpu-events-bd1-pair0-0 fully; setup_seconds across the eight BD1 samples; event_count across the eight BD2 samples). Other samples rely on verify_archive.py logic and the supplied verifier result.

Credential/privacy scan was pattern-based and not a comprehensive privacy review.
No GPU, MPI or harness tests were rerun; the 94-test log is historical.

findings.evidence: README says '`screen.py` and `job.sh` include earlier SDF machinery'. harness/job.sh is a Perlmutter batch wrapper: #SBATCH --account=lcls_g, pscratch task root, --time=00:30:00, job-name pr299-pilot, and it execs perlmutter_screen.py with "${1:?pilot or campaign}", so it can be submitted with a 'campaign' argument. The SDF leftovers are screen.py (Weka cache policy), nic.py (/sdf/data root) and test_nic.py.
findings.requested_change: Reword the README: describe job.sh as the earlier Perlmutter pilot/generic wrapper (30-minute allocation) that was not the campaign entry point and must not be submitted; name screen.py, nic.py and test_nic.py as the SDF-era helpers.
